    - heading "Understand Harmonic Motion" [level=2]
    - paragraph: "Harmonic motion is smooth repeating motion modelled by sine or cosine. In Harmonic Motion, that statement is the exact rule used on the labelled chart and in the three numerical examples. A useful rule is Harmonic model: y=A sin(omega t)+D. You can learn Harmonic Motion by trying one small example instead of long theory."
    - paragraph: Identify the midline. Measure amplitude from midline to peak. Read the time for one full cycle. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
    - paragraph: "In real life, swing: A small swing can look harmonic. Watch out: Measuring amplitude from peak to trough. Amplitude is from midline to peak."

  - article:
    - heading "Worked example" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Find x and v for a particle undergoing SHM with A = 2 at θ = 60° = π/3.
    - text: x(θ) = 2 cos(π/3) = 1
    - text: v(θ) = −2 sin(π/3) = −√3 ≈ −1.732
    - strong:
      - text: "Check on the lab: Set θ = 60°. You should see x ≈ 1.000 and v ≈ −1.732."
  - article:
    - heading "Common misconception" [level=2]:
      - text: Common misconception
    - text: Thinking the velocity is in phase with displacement.
    - paragraph: Because v(θ) = −sin θ, velocity is 90° out of phase. When x is maximum, velocity is zero. When velocity is maximum, displacement is zero.
